question.text: The indemnification provision in an IMA for Arjun Growth Fund specifies that the investment manager shall be indemnified by the fund for losses arising from:

answer.text: Fraud or willful misconduct by the investment manager
Any and all losses regardless of the cause
Actions taken in good faith and in accordance with the IMA, excluding gross negligence
Regulatory penalties imposed by SEBI for violations committed by the manager

explanation.text: The Logic: A typical IMA indemnification clause covers the investment manager for losses arising from actions taken in good faith and within the scope of the IMA, with explicit carve-outs for fraud, willful misconduct, and gross negligence. Indemnifying the manager for its own fraud or willful misconduct, or for unlimited losses regardless of cause, would be against public policy and unacceptable to investors; indemnifying against regulatory penalties for the manager's own SEBI violations would also be unenforceable. The Trap: The option for any and all losses seems protective of the manager but no reasonable investor or legal counsel would agree to unlimited indemnification — carve-outs for misconduct are industry standard. Note: The specific language of fund indemnification of the investment manager for good-faith actions under an IMA is not stated in the NISM Series XIX-A AIF (Category I and II) Distributors workbook pages checked; the framing here reflects general industry/legal practice for IMA indemnification clauses rather than a workbook citation.
